newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar extends gains on lower quota news.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar extends gains on lower quota news.

text.p: Sugar prices extended gains on Thursday helped by speculative buying after the Indian government cut free sale quotas, dealers said.

The government on Tuesday announced a free sale quota of 650,000 tonnes for January 1997 against the current month's 800,000 tonnes. Besides, it also extended the last date for selling December's quota from December 31 to January 10.
The quotas for February and March 1997 are 700,000 tonnes each. The quota for January 1996 had been 650,000 tonnes, while February and March had 625,000 each.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 11/18 rupees to 1,275/1,318 per quintal while M-30 climbed up by 5/10 rupees to 1,300/1,360. Sugar mill delivery looked up by 5 rupees to 1,215/1,225.
